newsitem.title: USA: S.F. stadium project would boost economy - study.
newsitem.headline: S.F. stadium project would boost economy - study.

text.p: A proposed $525 million stadium-mall complex would generate hundreds of millions of dollars each year in economic activity for the San Francisco area, a study released on Thursday said.

The study, prepared by accountants Deloitte & Touche, was released ahead of a June 3 special election on the San Francisco 49ers football stadium project. The ballot measure calls for the city to issue up to $100 million of bonds to help build the project.
The study made the following projections:

* The total one-time economic expenditures generated by construction of the proposed project will be $352 million. This economic activity is expected to generate $3.1 million in net tax revenue for San Francisco's general fund.
* Operation of the proposed project would generate $377.6 million in direct economic expenditures and about $233.2 million in indirect economic expenditures.

* Operation of the project will generate $1.0 million in net revenue for the city general fund annually. Operation of the project will generate $7.6 million in net revenue each year for other San Francisco agencies.

* A Super Bowl held in the proposed stadium would generate $61.1 million in direct economic activity and $50 million in indirect economic activity. This activity is expected to generate $2.3 million in net tax revenue for San Francisco's general fund.
